definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.

hypotheses: The torus has length 2*pi, the datum is real and mean-zero.
The horizon Q is positive and the nonnegative Sobolev regularity and initial norms are as stated.

inputs.statement: For Q>0, theta in (-1,0] and real mean-zero initial data U_0,W_0 in dot H^0 with ||U_0||_(dot H^0)+||W_0||_(dot H^0)<=B0, the two source twisted solutions z,y of z_k'=(i*k/2)sum_(k1+k2=k) exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*t)z_k1*z_k2 with these initial coefficients satisfy sup_(0<=t<=Q)||z(t)-y(t)||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^Q*||U_0-W_0||_(dot H^theta). The constants depend only on B0,theta. Since the untwisting multiplier is common and unitary, the same estimate holds for the physical source fields U,W.

hypotheses: The two data are real, mean-zero L^2 data and their dot H^0 norms sum to at most B0.

output.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

locals.declaration: Choose the source solution U with initial datum U0, whose existence is F001.
Fix a second datum b0 for the pairwise L^2 assertion.

argument.text: H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Fix a0 and temporarily assume L1: a0 is real, mean-zero, in H^gamma and ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Set U0(x)=-a0(-x), so hat U0(k)=-hat a0(-k). It is real and mean-zero and preserves all Fourier Sobolev norms. In particular ||U0||_(dot H^gamma)<=R and ||U0||_2<=R. Apply E001 with s=gamma,Q=T,U_0=U0. Its hypotheses hold by these norm facts and H001-H002. It supplies a unique continuous source flow U, a uniform homogeneous bound depending only on T,gamma,R, and smooth-approximation construction. Record its existence as F001.

produces.statement: There exists the unique source solution with initial datum U0 on [0,T], continuous in dot H^gamma, bounded there by a constant depending only on T,gamma,R, constructed by smooth approximation.

argument.text: Choose U from F001 and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). For smooth solutions u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx at (t,-x), so u_t+u_xxx=-UU_x=u*u_x=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The same equality follows distributionally by the reflection change of variables for the limiting solution. Fourier coefficients satisfy hat u(t)(k)=-hat U(t)(-k), hence all Sobolev norms, zero mean and reality are preserved. The comparison ||u||_(H^gamma)<=2^(gamma/2)||U||_(dot H^gamma) gives a bound A(T,gamma,R). Finite Fourier norm sums pass to the limit under smooth approximation, and their supremum gives the full bound; continuity gives it for every time. Uniqueness follows by applying the inverse reflection to two solutions, using the source coefficient formulation, equivalent to the distributional equation for continuous L^2 paths by testing each Fourier mode. Set v=S_(-t)u. Unit-modulus multipliers preserve its H^gamma norm. Differentiation for smooth data gives v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact u exists uniquely, sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R), v=S_(-t)u has the same bound, and for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

argument.text: For the smooth-data clause, temporarily assume L3: a0 is smooth. Apply E001 at every positive integer regularity s, with this same U0. Its finite higher norms and uniqueness make all these solutions coincide with U. Thus u is spatially smooth, and the equation supplies its time smoothness. Discharge L3 to obtain that conditional clause, and discharge L1 to obtain the stated assertion for every a0 in the ball. For the pairwise assertion fix arbitrary a0,b0 and temporarily assume L2: they are real mean-zero L^2 data whose norms sum to at most 2*R. Define W0=-b0(-x). E001 with s=0,Q=T supplies the source L^2 flows for each of U0,W0. Apply E002 with Q=T,theta=0,B0=2*R to those flows. Their zero mean, reality and norm sum are unchanged by reflection; theta=0 lies in (-1,0]. Its source common untwisting multiplier is an L^2 isometry, so E002 and reflection give sup||u_a0-u_b0||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. This includes the original H^gamma ball since each norm is <=R. Discharge L2. The constructions and bounds hold for every chosen datum; M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A. This proves the output assertion.
